## 2026-08-12T13:55:35.238Z
- Item: issue #4507 — Dead clicks: treat an in-flight network request as a liveness signal
- Conclusion: Valid enhancement proposal, but the requested signal is not available through the existing recorder hook for all dead-click users and safely adding it needs a deliberate instrumentation design.
- Labels: enhancement, feature/dead-clicks, team/analytics-platform
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4507
- Relevant files: `packages/browser/src/entrypoints/dead-clicks-autocapture.ts`, `packages/browser/src/__tests__/entrypoints/lazy-loaded-dead-clicks-autocapture.test.ts`, `packages/types/src/posthog-config.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/network-plugin.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/lazy-loaded-session-recorder.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/config.ts`, `packages/browser/src/utils/request-router.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/rrweb-plugins/patch.ts`
- Findings: `LazyLoadedDeadClicksAutocapture` currently stores timestamps only for mutations, scrolls, selection changes, and visibility changes. `_checkClicks` suppresses candidates with an in-window signal, otherwise requeues them until the mutation threshold and ultimately captures on an absolute timeout of `mutation_threshold_ms * 1.1`.; The dead-click configuration defaults the mutation threshold to 2500 ms, so an asynchronous UI whose DOM update occurs later can indeed be classified as dead despite a successful request.; The existing replay network plugin is not a general request-start feed. It is initialized only when replay is active and network capture is enabled; its `PerformanceObserver` callback observes resource entries after timing is available, while fetch/XHR wrapping is enabled only when request headers or bodies are being recorded.; The replay XHR instrumentation records its start timestamp in a `send` wrapper; the fetch/XHR code uses shared patch-chain handling because tracing headers and replay can both wrap the same primitives. A separate dead-click wrapper would re-enter this high-risk compatibility area.; Replay network capture already excludes PostHog ingestion requests using `requestRouter.isIngestionEndpoint`, with a path-based fallback for `/s/`, `/e/`, and `/i/`. `RequestRouter` accounts for rewritten ingestion URLs, but a new lazy bundle must feature-detect any newer-core API it calls.; The dead-click detector is itself a lazy-loaded entrypoint. The incident guidance requires old-core/new-bundle compatibility when adding cross-boundary APIs or assumptions.; Existing unit tests already exercise suppression and timeout behavior for mutation, scroll, selection, and visibility signals, providing a focused place to add the proposed signal tests.
- Fix assessment: The behavioral change is narrow, but request-start observation cannot simply reuse the existing replay hook without missing users and requests. Adding or altering fetch/XHR instrumentation has a documented high compatibility risk, while changing the lazy entrypoint must remain compatible with older SDK cores. The required timing window and scope are also not specified.

## 2026-08-12T14:00:39.623Z
- Item: issue #4507 — Dead clicks: treat an in-flight network request as a liveness signal
- Conclusion: Valid dead-click detection enhancement, but request-start instrumentation needs an explicit scope and high-risk compatibility review before implementation.
- Labels: enhancement, feature/dead-clicks, team/analytics-platform
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4507
- Relevant files: `packages/browser/src/entrypoints/dead-clicks-autocapture.ts`, `packages/browser/src/__tests__/entrypoints/lazy-loaded-dead-clicks-autocapture.test.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/dead-clicks-autocapture.ts`, `packages/types/src/posthog-config.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/network-plugin.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/lazy-loaded-session-recorder.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/config.ts`, `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/rrweb-plugins/patch.ts`, `packages/browser/src/utils/request-router.ts`
- Findings: The lazy dead-click detector records timestamps for mutation, scroll, selection, and visibility signals. `_checkClicks` suppresses candidates with an in-window signal, otherwise requeues until a configured mutation threshold of 2500ms and captures on an absolute timeout of threshold × 1.1.; Visibility changes are already suppress-only: they prevent a dead event but are not evidence used to capture one. A network-start signal can follow that established behavior.; The dead-click extension is lazy-loaded via `initDeadClicksAutocapture`, so new calls from the entrypoint to newer core APIs must be optional for old pinned cores receiving the latest extension bundle.; Replay network capture is not a universal request-start source. It is initialized only when replay network capture is enabled; its PerformanceObserver consumes resource entries, while fetch/XHR wrapping is only enabled when replay headers or bodies are recorded.; The replay fetch and XHR wrappers are sensitive compatibility code. They use a shared patch-chain helper because tracing headers and replay may both patch the same globals; the fetch path explicitly preserves original `fetch(url, init)` arguments to avoid Safari ReadableStream-upload failures.; Replay excludes PostHog ingestion through a feature-detected `requestRouter.isIngestionEndpoint` callback and a fallback based on `/s/`, `/e/`, and `/i/` paths. `RequestRouter` tracks rewritten ingestion endpoints, so a new signal must preserve equivalent exclusions.
- Fix assessment: The behavioral rule is narrow, but observing request start for all dead-click users requires fetch/XHR patching independent of replay. Those globals already have chained wrappers and documented WebKit/body-type failure modes, while the detector is a lazy-loaded bundle that must remain compatible with old cores. The request window and swipe scope are also unspecified.

## 2026-08-14T08:29:47.120Z
- Item: issue #4522 — Session replay: uncaught TypeError on stop() when observe() returned undefined after a swallowed observer-init error — recorder is then permanently broken for the session
- Conclusion: Confirmed session-replay teardown bug in the bundled rrweb recorder.
- Labels: feature/replay, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4522
- Relevant files: `packages/browser/src/extensions/replay/external/lazy-loaded-session-recorder.ts`, `packages/browser/src/__tests__/extensions/replay/lazy-sessionrecording.test.ts`, `packages/rrweb/rrweb/src/record/index.ts`, `packages/rrweb/rrweb/src/record/error-handler.ts`, `packages/rrweb/rrweb/src/record/observer.ts`, `packages/rrweb/rrweb/src/utils.ts`, `packages/rrweb/rrweb/test/record/error-handler.test.ts`, `packages/rrweb/README.md`
- Findings: LazyLoadedSessionRecording supplies an error handler that returns true only for context === 'rrweb', intentionally swallowing recorder-owned exceptions while preserving host-operation exceptions.; callbackWrapper() returns undefined when its callback throws and the registered handler returns true, despite being cast back to the original callback type.; record/index.ts pushes observe(document) directly into handlers and likewise pushes the iframe observe result into both handlers and iframeObserverCleanups without a runtime function check.; The record stop closure runs handlers.forEach((h) => callSafely(h)), while callSafely() immediately executes fn() and only suppresses SecurityError. A runtime undefined handler therefore throws TypeError and aborts the rest of teardown.; initObservers() initializes observers sequentially and returns its aggregate cleanup only after all setup completes. If a later initializer throws, cleanups for earlier successfully initialized observers are not returned to record(), so insertion/call guards alone do not establish complete cleanup.; Current tests verify that the lazy recorder configures an error handler and that callbackWrapper swallows errors when its handler returns true, but no inspected test exercises a swallowed initObservers failure followed by stop and restart.; Replay incident review: this is a lazy-loaded bundle path, but the proposed repair need not change the core/extension API or persisted-state shape. It also reaches forced-idle and session-rotation stop paths; no recording-volume change is intended, but those scenario tests should protect that invariant.
- Fix assessment: The immediate uncaught TypeError has a small defensive fix, but only filtering/ignoring non-function handlers can leave observers installed before a late initObservers failure. A safe repair needs a focused regression test and exception-safe cleanup for successfully initialized observer resources, without broadening the error-swallowing policy.

## 2026-08-14T11:52:51.013Z
- Item: issue #4524 — Socket.dev supply-chain score below 50 on recent posthog-js releases, failing downstream CI supply-chain gates
- Conclusion: Credible downstream supply-chain-gate compatibility report, but the repository cannot establish why Socket.dev assigns these scores or justify a metadata/release-process change yet.
- Labels: question, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4524
- Relevant files: `packages/browser/package.json`, `packages/node/package.json`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- Findings: `packages/browser/package.json` identifies the package as `posthog-js` at version `1.417.0`, matching the issue's cited latest browser SDK version, and declares `author` as `engineering@posthog.com`.; `posthog-js` deliberately publishes built browser distributions, React distributions, and package entrypoint metadata through its `files` allowlist; the repository alone does not establish the unpacked size of the published npm tarball or whether size affects Socket's score.; The release workflow requires an approved `NPM Release` environment before version bumping, then publishes `posthog-js` from GitHub Actions with `id-token: write` permission and `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true`.; `posthog-node` has different package metadata, including a structured `PostHog` author object and a substantially narrower `files` allowlist, so its reported higher external score is not sufficient to isolate one causal difference.; No Socket.dev integration, score configuration, or documented mapping from Socket supply-chain axes to repository-controlled settings was found in the inspected repository files.
- Fix assessment: The report identifies an external vendor score, not a reproducible SDK defect. The repository already uses approval-gated GitHub Actions publishing with npm provenance; changing package metadata, tarball contents, or release cadence without Socket's specific rationale would be speculative and could disrupt consumers or releases.

## 2026-08-14T12:22:54.248Z
- Item: issue #4525 — perf(react-native): useFeatureFlags / useFeatureFlag re-read the full flag store on every render
- Conclusion: Confirmed React Native performance bug with a small, behavior-preserving fix.
- Labels: react-native, feature/flags, team/client-libraries
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4525
- Relevant files: `packages/react-native/src/hooks/useFeatureFlags.ts`, `packages/react-native/src/hooks/useFeatureFlag.ts`, `packages/react-native/src/hooks/useFeatureFlagResult.ts`, `packages/react-native/test/useFeatureFlagResult.spec.ts`, `packages/core/src/posthog-core.ts`, `packages/react/src/hooks/useFeatureFlagEnabled.ts`, `packages/react/src/hooks/useActiveFeatureFlags.ts`
- Findings: `useFeatureFlags` currently initializes state with `posthog?.getFeatureFlags()` directly, and `useFeatureFlag` does the same with `posthog?.getFeatureFlag(flag)`, confirming both getters are evaluated during every render.; Each reported hook's existing effect explicitly rereads the getter when its dependencies change and subscribes through `onFeatureFlags`, so a lazy initializer changes only discarded rerender work, not the initial value or update paths.; `PostHogCore.getFeatureFlags()` calls `getFeatureFlagDetails()`, and `getKnownFeatureFlagDetails()` calls `normalizeFlagsResponse()` whenever stored flag details exist. `getFeatureFlag()` similarly reads feature-flag details through `_getFeatureFlagResult`, so avoiding unnecessary hook calls avoids synchronous flag-store processing.; `@posthog/react` already uses lazy state initialization in `useFeatureFlagEnabled` and `useActiveFeatureFlags`, matching the proposed React pattern.; There are no focused tests for the two reported React Native hooks. `useFeatureFlagResult` has an established React hook test setup that can be used as a minimal precedent for adding rerender regression coverage.; `useFeatureFlagResult` also has an eager getter state initializer, but it is outside the issue's explicitly requested scope and should not be changed incidentally without corresponding coverage and maintainer agreement.
- Fix assessment: Wrapping the two existing initial reads in lazy `useState` initializer functions is a two-line behavioral no-op after mount. Existing effects retain client-change, flag-change, reload, and reset handling.
- PR: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/4526

## 2026-08-18T07:33:26.765Z
- Item: issue #4546 — source map with `deleteAfterUpload` doesn't strip sourcemap comments from css files
- Conclusion: Confirmed scope gap in the Turbopack sourcemap-comment cleanup: it only processes JavaScript files, so dangling CSS source map references remain after deletion.
- Labels: feature/error-tracking, team/error-tracking
- URL: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/issues/4546
- Relevant files: `packages/nextjs-config/src/config.ts`, `packages/nextjs-config/src/strip-sourcemap-comments.ts`, `packages/nextjs-config/src/strip-sourcemap-comments.spec.ts`, `packages/nextjs-config/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/webpack-plugin/src/index.ts`
- Findings: `withCompilerConfig` calls `stripDanglingSourceMapComments` after sourcemap upload only when Turbopack is enabled and `deleteAfterUpload` is true.; `stripDanglingSourceMapComments` currently calls `listJsFiles`, whose extension filter is limited to `.js`, `.mjs`, and `.cjs`; no `.css` assets are inspected.; The current matcher only recognizes JavaScript line comments (`//# sourceMappingURL=...`), not CSS block comments (`/*# sourceMappingURL=... */`).; The existing tests cover JavaScript cleanup, retained existing maps, inline maps, remote maps, CRLF, and module extensions, but contain no CSS fixture.; `packages/nextjs-config/CHANGELOG.md` confirms #3764 shipped in 1.9.68 specifically as a Turbopack dangling-comment cleanup.; The webpack plugin already suppresses SourceMapDevToolPlugin comment emission with `append: false` when `deleteAfterUpload` is enabled, but it separately deletes emitted CSS map files after upload.
- Fix assessment: The omission is localized to the Next.js Turbopack cleanup helper. A small extension to inspect CSS files and remove only dangling local CSS mapping comments, backed by focused tests, addresses the reported behavior without changing upload or deletion semantics.
- PR: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/4547
